_comment: TEMPLATE - not a real suite. Copy lines from here into your manifest.jsonl and delete the _comment keys. Every line is one JSON object; JSON Lines has no comment syntax, so the _comment key is the convention used here.

MINIMAL LINK-ONLY CASE, as authored by hand. No image_sha256 yet: you have not downloaded the file, so you cannot know it. Run `agribench fetch --pin` and the digest is written back here automatically.

SAME CASE AFTER PINNING. image_sha256 is filled in and `image` now names the content-addressed file. From here on every download is verified against this digest, so a link that starts serving different bytes is rejected instead of silently scored.

FULLY ATTRIBUTED LINK-ONLY CASE. source_page and credit are optional but strongly encouraged: they are what lets a reader check the label against the original context, and what you will want if the origin ever asks how their image is being used.
credit: Example Plant Clinic, used by reference only
notes: Whole-plant view, late stage. Label confirmed against the source page caption.

_comment: BUNDLED CASE for contrast. distribution defaults to bundled, the licence must be redistributable (CC0, CC-BY, MIT, Apache-2.0, public-domain), and image_sha256 is mandatory because you already have the bytes.

SOURCE-ONLY CASE. Neither redistributable nor individually addressable: its publisher ships an archive or a parquet file, so there is no URL that returns this one image. The manifest records the digest and names the dataset; the operator downloads that dataset from the publisher and stages this file out of it by content digest. Licence may be anything, including unknown -- the case claims no redistribution right at all.
notes: Staged with `agribench stage --from <extracted archive>`; matched by digest, not filename.
